title: GSF Commander Batsuuri Visits Artibonite to Assess Sri Lankan Contingent Operations
detail: Major General Erdenebat Batsuuri, Force Commander of the UN-backed Gang Suppression Force, visited Artibonite department on August 13, 2026 to evaluate the newly landed Sri Lankan contingent's operations in Gonaïves, one week after its August 6 arrival. Batsuuri met with the Sri Lankan contingent commander and local officials — including the vice departmental delegate, the Mayor of Gonaïves, and the Bishop of Gonaïves — to discuss the security situation, operational coordination, and community relations in a department that has recorded 381 killings (25.7% of Haiti's 2026 national total) amid expanding Gran Grif and Kokorat San Ras gang activity.

media.caption: GSF Commander Maj. Gen. Erdenebat Batsuuri visits Gonaïves, Artibonite

title: Catholic Bishops, Rights Groups Warn TPS Termination Puts 330,000+ Haitians at Deportation Risk
detail: With Haiti's Temporary Protected Status formally terminated August 5, 2026 following the Supreme Court's June 25 ruling, more than 330,000 Haitian TPS holders in the US now face potential deportation into a country under a Level 4 'do not travel' advisory. A Bloomberg report (Aug 12) documented fears that deportees would be seen by gangs as wealthy 'outside' targets, citing the February 2026 case of four Haitian women deported from Puerto Rico who were later kidnapped and found beheaded. On August 13, Catholic bishops — including Bishop Brendan J. Cahill and Cardinal Chibly Langlois of Haiti — met with US senators urging passage of a bipartisan TPS extension bill (passed by the House, not yet scheduled for a Senate vote) through 2029, with Cahill calling the termination 'a moral crisis.'

media.caption: Children in a Port-au-Prince displacement camp, July 31, 2026, as TPS termination raises deportation fears

title: Port-au-Prince Holds First Criminal Assizes Since 2018
detail: Port-au-Prince's criminal court convened Assizes proceedings on August 13, 2026 — the first since 2018 — with support from BINUH and coordination by the Port-au-Prince Criminal Justice System Monitoring Committee, HaitiLibre reported August 17. The long-delayed jury-trial sessions aim to reduce chronic pretrial detention and prison overcrowding, both worsened by years of judicial paralysis amid the gang crisis, marking a rare functioning-institution milestone for Haiti's collapsed justice system.

media.caption: Port-au-Prince holds first Criminal Assizes since 2018, backed by BINUH
